body:
Okay so even though I said so two weeks ago I'm only looking into it now, and the bug seems to actually be way more generic than just broadcasting inputs over output with a 0-dim input. As an example of an alternative where this still happens, you can try to run `torch.foo(torch.rand((5, 5, 5, 5, 5)), torch.rand((5, 5)), torch.rand((5, 5, 5)))`.

From testing with various other possible dimensions, the general rule seems to be something like "the inputs do not all have equal dimensions, and the output has dimension at least 2 greater than the max input dimension". I created a local `foo2` function that takes in 4 input tensors rather than just 2, and the rule seems to hold for it, too: if every input tensor has the same dimension everything works fine, otherwise if the output dimension is at least 2 greater than the maximum input dimension we segfault.

So I'm inclined to agree that the problem is in the TI implementation of the loop somewhere, and would have to dig into it.

That said, when I ran these tests I got the following general shape of warning message:
```
UserWarning: An output with one or more elements was resized since it had shape [5, 5, 5], which does not match the required output shape [5, 5]. This behavior is deprecated, and in a future PyTorch release outputs will not be resized unless they have zero elements. You can explicitly reuse an out tensor t by resizing it, inplace, to zero elements with t.resize_(0).
```

What will the new behaviour be? That change alone might be sufficient to fix this bug too, depending on what the underlying cause is. @nikitaved do you know?

Hey, @redmagnos , sorry for the delay. This warning is about output being broadcasted over input, so you have several elements in the input that correspond to the same element in the output. Should not be a problem in the context of `foo`.

@nikitaved Oh I know it's not a problem for this case. What I meant was that the warning specifically said that the functionality of resizing the output to match the input like that will no longer be supported in the future, and depending on how that's implemented, it might solve the issue all on its own (since the issue seems to be exactly related to the relative sizes of the tensors). But again, it might also not, which is why I ask what the actual new behaviour in the future will be.

In my repro it is the shape `shape : [torch.Size([5, 5, 5]), torch.Size([]), torch.Size([5])]` that causes a segfault. Here, two inputs of smaller sizes broadcast over an output of a larger size, so no warning is triggered as `resize` is not needed. This case is well-defined and should not segfault.

Right, I understand this; that shape _also_ causes the segfault for me, any shapes where the output is 2+ larger than the inputs and the inputs are not the same size segfault, and the one you suggest is just a special case of this general rule.

However, with the current version of pyTorch I have installed the warning _is_ triggered even in those cases. If what you mean here is that for cases where the output is larger than the inputs the warning will merely be silenced and the behaviour will not change, then I will resume looking into the bug. That is the question I am asking, is what future behaviour changes there will be for this and similar cases, if any.

I see no warnings, the warning is about `resize` for the output. Once output is large enough, there is no need in resizing it. But let me double-check it.... Silent resizes might introduce bugs and/or potentially memory leaks, so this is what is going to be changed in the future I guess.

There is even simpler repro (@redmagnos, no warnings here):

```python
In [1]: import torch

In [2]: x = torch.rand(2)

In [3]: y = torch.rand(())

In [4]: z = torch.rand(2, 2, 2)

In [5]: torch.add(x, y, out=z)
Segmentation fault (core dumped)

```
Which renders ALL out variants as unsafe.
@redmagnos , I speculate the issue could be in the `loop_2d` function of the TensorIterator and/or broadcasting.
